message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I'll bid $120. That clears the minimum and nets $30 after mortgaging the property. This also blocks p4 from completing a second green.

p4 is in jail with $763 cash and a strong light blue set. Pacific Avenue is mortgaged by p1, so no player can complete the green monopoly yet.

I'm currently on Pennsylvania Avenue, which p4 owns but has mortgaged. That property doesn't collect rent, so I'm safe there. I'm positioned before the dark blue properties, so future rolls will likely land me near Park Place and Boardwalk.

I can liquidate my pink houses for roughly $600. Combined with my cash, I have about $1326 available. That covers Park Place but not Boardwalk.

Mortgaging North Carolina immediately would raise cash to about $756, giving a slightly better buffer for future dark blue rent. I'm considering whether to jump bid and force p4 to make a decision.

I'll keep bidding the minimum. Dropping now would let p4 win for $119 and still net $31 after mortgaging, giving them a cheap second green. I'll push the bid to $150.

A $150 bid nets zero cash after mortgaging, but blocking p4 from completing the green monopoly is a strong strategic reason to continue. With two greens, p4 could trade with p1 for Pacific Avenue and finish the set. p1 is nearly bankrupt and cannot afford to pay for that trade.

Splitting the green set three ways is the best outcome. I should stop at $150 and mortgage immediately. Bidding higher would permanently reduce cash needed for future rent.

Full liquidation plus an immediate mortgage leaves $1476 available. That covers Park Place at $1100 even if I bid up to $376. Boardwalk remains impossible regardless. The real constraint is the denial value, not Boardwalk. Bidding $150 and mortgaging North Carolina preserves my cash at $726 while blocking p4 from completing a second green.
